findings.title: Target process inherits an uncontrolled handle set across the helper trust boundary.
findings.evidence: src/platform/windows/job-object.ts:66,103-123 calls CreateProcessW with inherit=true and a STARTUPINFO, without STARTUPINFOEX/PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_HANDLE_LIST; only three pipe handles are passed through SetHandleInformation and its return values are ignored. The helper's own standard handles and any other inheritable helper handles are therefore eligible for inheritance.
findings.impact: A target capable of enumerating its inherited handle table can access the helper's control streams or unrelated inherited handles, allowing control-frame spoofing/consumption and cross-process handle disclosure. This violates the explicit target/control-channel separation requirement even though the disposable proof only exercised target stdout spoofing.
findings.remediation: Launch with an explicit inherited-handle allowlist (STARTUPINFOEX PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_HANDLE_LIST) or an equivalent non-inheriting design; fail closed when handle-isolation setup fails and check every handle-flag operation.
findings.verification: Add a bounded Windows proof that inspects the target's inherited handles/standard streams and demonstrates that only the target stdin/stdout/stderr handles are present and helper control frames cannot be read or written by the target.

findings.title: Native launch setup failure can strand an unowned suspended process.
findings.evidence: src/platform/windows/job-object.ts:132-143 closes pi.hThread/pi.hProcess after CreateJobObjectW, SetInformationJobObject, or AssignProcessToJobObject failure; the job=zero path at line 132 and the catch path call TerminateJobObject on an empty/unassigned Job but never call TerminateProcess(pi.hProcess).
findings.impact: A native-policy/API failure can leave the CREATE_SUSPENDED target alive indefinitely outside the Job. Repeated failures consume process and kernel resources and violate the fail-closed managed-launch boundary.
findings.remediation: Track whether assignment completed and explicitly terminate the suspended process with its held process handle on every pre-assignment failure before closing handles; verify the process handle signals or report cleanup failure.
findings.verification: Inject or reproduce CreateJobObjectW, SetInformationJobObject, and AssignProcessToJobObject failures and assert no target PID remains after the bounded cleanup path.

findings.title: Malformed control or launch-frame timeout does not reliably close the Job.
findings.evidence: The helper's ConvertFrom-Json catch at src/platform/windows/job-object.ts:218-219 emits an error frame and continues. waitForFrame at lines 367-381 only removes a timed-out waiter; managedLaunch awaits readyPromise at lines 472-474 without a timeout cleanup path, while failHandle at lines 357-365 marks the handle closed and rejects waiters without closing or killing the helper.
findings.impact: A malformed/desynchronized control stream or a helper that never produces its attached frame can leave the opaque Job owner and target alive after the caller has lost a usable attachment. This contradicts the documented malformed-control/fatal-failure cleanup guarantee and creates a local custody/resource leak.
findings.remediation: Treat malformed control and bounded protocol timeouts as fatal: terminate/close the helper so kill-on-close executes, await bounded helper exit, and surface a retryable failure only after the target absence/cleanup postcondition is established.
findings.verification: Bounded proofs for malformed JSON, oversized/incomplete frames, and missing attached response must prove helper exit, target absence, and no unrelated process impact.
